newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves fall to $15.583 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves fall to $15.583 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves fell $303 million, or 1.91 percent, to $15.583 billion in the week to January 7, according to figures released by the Central Bank.
Reserves were down from $15.886 billion on April 14, the bank's weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
This was the third consecutive weekly fall but since the start of the year reserves have risen $404 million, with a peak at $15.967 billion.
Last year, reserves rose $5.5 billion, or 57 percent, to $15.179 billion, boosted by large capital inflows stemming from high international oil prices.
This overshot the government's original target of growth by only $1.5 billion in 1996, as part of Venezuela's IMF-supported economic adjustment program launched in mid-April.
Government officials have forecast that reserves will grow to $20 billion by the end of 1997.
